translations.answer: Do not compile or run the Gazebo simulation module on onboard computers, nor start the legged_cheater_controller on real hardware, as it depends on simulation truth states. The real machine should start hardware interfaces, real state estimation, and legged_controller, and gradually enable targets and gains in low-risk conditions.
translations.applicability: Applicable to legged_control; other frameworks should explicitly define the boundary between simulation truth states and real measured states.
translations.credibility.rationale: The issue has been closed, the environment is clear and there is no conflict. It has been formally documented or independently reproducible with precise reference.
translations.details.attempts.0: Inherit LeggedHW and implement read()/write() functions.
translations.details.attempts.1: Follow the pattern of unitree_description to generate URDF and maintain joint/link naming conventions.
translations.details.attempts.2: Start the real machine only with real state estimation and legged_controller.
translations.details.diagnostics.0: Check the hardware interfaces, description files, controllers, and state estimation directories against the official repository directory.
translations.details.effective_fixes.0: Isolate platform differences via ros-control, and separate simulation from hardware in official startup order.
translations.details.environments.0: ROS/ros-control; OCS2; A1; author used a 11th Gen NUC, NMPC frequency close to 200 Hz; the repository currently states it is stopped from maintenance.
translations.details.limits.0: The repository is no longer maintained; versions, dependencies, and safety boundaries must be re-verified against the current fork.
translations.details.outcomes.0: The official README lists multiple labs running on A1, with historical records of 2 hours to 1 day; the author's code structure is consistent with the repository.
translations.details.problem_statements.0: What is the minimum compatible boundary when migrating legged_control to a custom robot?
translations.details.problem_statements.1: Why can't simulation controller and real controller be mixed?
translations.details.safety_notes.0: The official README explicitly states that real machines cannot start the cheater controller; initial control should use a cradle, low gain, limit force, and emergency stop.
translations.details.suspected_causes.0: Hardware read/write interfaces and joint naming conventions do not meet framework assumptions.
translations.details.suspected_causes.1: Using simulation truth states or simulation load in real machine processes.
translations.details.symptoms.0: Direct modification of the main repository makes hardware compatibility maintenance difficult.
translations.details.symptoms.1: Starting the real machine with the cheater controller or running Gazebo on onboard hardware causes incorrect states or resource risks.
translations.media_summaries.0: The main framework diagram shows the trajectory trajectory → NMPC → WBC → forward force torque + low gain PD, and IMU/actuator states → Kalman filter; the repository README text is consistent with this.
translations.source.locator: Official README Build / Quick Start hardware warning, main framework and state estimation description in the text.
